stocks.note: Numbers as of market close April 30th.
stocks.news:
Wall Street closed April with its biggest monthly gain since 2020. The S&P notched +10% on the month, with NASDAQ matching that pace, both their best month since the 2020 pandemic rebound. Big Tech earnings carried the load past the oil shock and Fed-on-hold backdrop.

Apple (AAPL +0.44%) reported after the bell, beating Wall Street with stronger profits even as iPhone sales slowed. Tim Cook is still stepping down this September, with SVP John Ternus taking the chair. Industrials led Thursday's session, with the Dow tacking on +796 points in a single day. Alphabet posted its best month since October 2004.

economy.commentary:
🎭 The truth about who's running the global economy: Q1 2026 GDP just printed at 2% growth, quadruple last quarter's 0.5%. The engine? Business investment in AI, up 8.7%. Tech giants are now expected to spend roughly $1 trillion on AI through 2027. That's not abstract. It's a big reason the U.S. still towers over the rest of the world.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on April 30th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto held steady into month-end, with all three majors green. The bigger story: Elon Musk took the stand in the Musk vs. Altman case and called "most" crypto coins scams, which is interesting given Tesla still holds 11,509 BTC (~$1B). It also came out that OpenAI considered launching its own crypto coin in 2018, but Musk blocked it.

Meanwhile, Gemini (GEMI +7.25%) won CFTC approval to run its own derivatives clearinghouse, opening the door to launching perpetual futures (crypto contracts with no expiration). Spot trading is volatile with prices, but derivatives can give exchanges steadier revenue. The infrastructure layer keeps building out even as the spot crowd cools.

real_estate.homebuilder: Best Stock Month Since 2020, But Spring Housing Still Walking; The U.S. Towers Globally
real_estate.commentary:
Wall Street just notched its biggest month since 2020, with the S&P up over 10% in April. Q1 GDP came in healthy at 2%, AI investment doing the heavy lifting. But the local spring rebound is still walking, not running. With the 30-year fixed parked at 6.45%, buyers are taking their time and sellers are holding firm. The structural story remains the same nationally: spring housing rebound is stalling for the second year, homeowners locked into 3% rates aren't moving, and inventory keeps piling up. But purchase applications are still up 21% YoY, which means the buyers at the door right now have already accepted the rate environment. They're qualified and committed.
